suggestions.expectation: commit.diff shows HEAD is a commit whose subject starts with docs(session): and the fix(finder) commit is an ancestor
suggestions.reason: When the run splits its work into two docs(session) commits, commit.diff (HEAD only) captures the trivial README follow-up and none of the entry. Expectations 1, 6 and 7 all read commit.diff, so the discriminating content lives in HEAD~1 and is invisible to them; expectation 6 only failed because the grader also checked the fixture. Consider capturing `git diff <fix-sha>..HEAD` (everything since the recorded commit) instead of `git show HEAD`, or add an expectation that the record lands in a single docs(session) commit.

suggestions.expectation: session-file.md's entry Notes state how the fix's claim was verified (a driver run, a byte comparison or swiftc), and transcript.md shows that verification command was actually run
suggestions.reason: Good, discriminating expectation — it caught the run asserting a byte comparison it never ran. Keep it. One tightening: the run put the verification method on the Files line and in the Narrative, not in Notes; decide whether the expectation means the Notes field specifically or the entry as a whole, since a lenient grader could pass the first clause.

No expectation checks that the session-index line in docs/sessions/README.md got committed (the session tool regenerates it on every append). This run committed it as a separate commit; a run that forgot it would leave a dirty tree — caught by expectation 4's empty-status check — but a run that committed it with `git add -A` would pass expectation 4 and fail 7. Worth an explicit check that README.md is in the docs(session) commit range, since it is the cheapest thing to miss.

The run's sweep for stale docs stopped at OVERVIEW because that is the only file the skill names by example. Expectation 6 is the right check for this, but its wording ('commit.diff shows …') can only be satisfied if the sweep lands in HEAD; pair it with the range-diff change above.

eval_feedback.overall: Five of seven pass. The two failures are real and discriminating: an unverified 'byte-identical' claim (no comparison command was run) and an incomplete stale-doc sweep (two nested docs still say the asset is stale). The main eval weakness is that three expectations read commit.diff = HEAD only, which the two-commit split rendered nearly empty; capture the range since the fix commit instead.
